newsitem.title: ITALY: One in five Italians too poor for Xmas gifts - survey.
newsitem.headline: One in five Italians too poor for Xmas gifts - survey.

text.p: One in five Italians feels too poor to give Christmas gifts this year, a survey said on Tuesday.
The poll, conducted by the ASM group among 1,000 Italians, found 21 percent of people were not planning to give presents and 55 percent would only give useful gifts.
Only 16 percent of Italians, mostly teenagers, would not change the traditional Christmas gift ritual, the survey said.

Italy is an affluent society and many people are big savers, but tax hikes included in an 62.5 trillion lire ($41 billion) austerity budget for 1997, and a new "euro-tax" to help Italy qualify for a European single currency, have increased worries.
The survey found that 20 percent of Italians -- a quarter of whom live in the south -- already considered themselves very poor and 43 percent felt they would soon become so. ($1=1525 Lire)
